MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 28? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 3
   C. 7
   D. 5

2. Which list shows all the factors of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15
   B. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   C. 1, 2, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   D. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30

3. What is the next number in the pattern 3, 7, 11, 15, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 19
   B. 23
   C. 20
   D. 18

4. In the number 3,850, the digit 8 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Thousands
   B. Tens
   C. Hundreds
   D. Ones

5. Which number is written in words as "three thousand, four hundred and fifty"? (1 mark)
   A. 34,500
   B. 3,450
   C. 345
   D. 3,540

6. Work out 5,684 + 3,749. (1 mark)
   A. 9,443
   B. 9,333
   C. 8,323
   D. 9,433

7. Work out 3,425 + 2,318. (1 mark)
   A. 5,733
   B. 5,753
   C. 5,643
   D. 5,743

8. Which number must be added to 2,318 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 8,061
   B. 3,425
   C. 3,415
   D. 3,525

9. What is the rule of the pattern 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500? (1 mark)
   A. add 1,000
   B. subtract 500
   C. add 500
   D. add 2,000

10. Work out 7,305 + 2,489. (1 mark)
   A. 9,784
   B. 9,694
   C. 9,794
   D. 9,804

11. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,280
   B. 5,380
   C. 5,290
   D. 5,270

12. What is 27 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 5,400
   B. 540
   C. 47
   D. 54

13. Work out 18 × 35. (1 mark)
   A. 144
   B. 630
   C. 640
   D. 620

14. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 800
   B. 900
   C. 700
   D. 8,000

15. What is 61 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 6
   B. 7 remainder 12
   C. 8 remainder 5
   D. 9 remainder 5

16. What is 83 ÷ 9? (1 mark)
   A. 10 remainder 2
   B. 9 remainder 2
   C. 9 remainder 3
   D. 8 remainder 11

17. 47 mangoes are shared equally among 6 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 1
   C. 6
   D. 5

18. Change 17/5 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/5
   B. 3 3/5
   C. 4 2/5
   D. 2 3/5

19. Which decimal is equal to 0.7? (1 mark)
   A. 0.71
   B. 0.70
   C. 0.07
   D. 7.0

20. If y = 3, what is the value of 8 − y? (1 mark)
   A. 83
   B. 11
   C. 5
   D. 24

21. Simplify 2c + 3d + 4c. (1 mark)
   A. 2c + 7d
   B. 6c + 7d
   C. 6c + 3d
   D. 9cd

22. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 28 cm
   B. 40 cm
   C. 13 cm
   D. 26 cm

23. A cuboid has a volume of 48 blocks. One layer has 8 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 40
   C. 6
   D. 56

24. Cuboid A is 4 by 3 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 3 by 3 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid B
   B. It cannot be told
   C. They are equal
   D. Cuboid A

25. What is 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 L
   B. 4 L
   C. 3 1/2 L
   D. 4 1/4 L

26. A shopper buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1 1/4 kg
   B. 1 kg
   C. 1 1/2 kg
   D. 5/8 kg

27. A big sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. What does this tell us? (1 mark)
   A. Size does not tell us the mass
   B. Big things are always heavy
   C. Mass is measured in metres
   D. Small things are always light

28. What is 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 3/4 kg
   D. 4 kg

29. In which direction do shadows point in the early morning? (1 mark)
   A. Towards the east
   B. Towards the west
   C. They do not point anywhere
   D. Straight up

30. One unit costs Ksh 130. What is the cost of 6 loaves of bread? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 650
   B. Ksh 136
   C. Ksh 790
   D. Ksh 780

31. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 1,200, Ksh 2,350 and Ksh 875. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 4,325
   B. Ksh 4,425
   C. Ksh 4,525
   D. Ksh 4,435

32. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 95, Ksh 140 and Ksh 260. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 395
   B. Ksh 505
   C. Ksh 495
   D. Ksh 595

33. Musa has one Ksh 100 note, one Ksh 50 note and two Ksh 20 coins. How much money does he have? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 150
   B. Ksh 210
   C. Ksh 170
   D. Ksh 190

34. How many cents are in Ksh 8? (1 mark)
   A. 8,000 cents
   B. 800 cents
   C. 108 cents
   D. 80 cents

35. You face the door and make a half turn. What do you face now? (1 mark)
   A. The ceiling
   B. The door
   C. The back wall
   D. The left wall only

36. An angle that is smaller than a right angle looks like (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a corner that is more open than a square corner
   C. a circle
   D. a corner that is more closed than a square corner

37. Which fold gives a line of symmetry of a rectangle that is not a square? (1 mark)
   A. Across the middle from side to side
   B. From one corner to the middle of the opposite long side
   C. Along a diagonal
   D. Along one of the short sides

38. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. mango
   B. pawpaw
   C. orange
   D. banana

39. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are NOT pawpaw? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 11
   C. 1
   D. 9

40. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many more are there of matatu than of boda boda? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 4
   C. 7
   D. 5

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write 583 in words. (2 marks)

42. A tailor has 3 m 60 cm of cloth and uses 1 m 85 cm. How much cloth is left? (3 marks)

43. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250. (3 marks)

44. A book cover has 12 rows of 9 squares. A notebook cover has 10 rows of 10 squares. Which cover is larger and by how many squares? (4 marks)

45. A ribbon is 5 m 20 cm long. A piece 2 m 75 cm long is cut off. How much ribbon is left? (3 marks)

46. A rectangular field is 45 m long and 30 m wide. (a) Find its perimeter. (b) A farmer wants to fence it but leaves two gates of 3 m each. How many metres of fence does he need? (5 marks)

47. Work out 4 L − 1 3/4 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

48. How can you tell that a cuboid is a cube? Give one example of each from everyday life. (3 marks)

49. For the number 4,835: (a) write it in expanded form, (b) give the total value of the digit 8, (c) round it to the nearest ten, (d) say whether it is even or odd. (5 marks)

50. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books were left? Check your answer. (4 marks)

51. Kamau buys 15 packets of sweets and each packet has 40 sweets. How many sweets does he have? (2 marks)

52. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and the cuboid has 4 layers. Find the volume. Then find the volume if 2 more layers are added. (4 marks)

53. A box is packed with cubes in layers. Each layer has 8 cubes along the length and 5 cubes across the width. There are 4 layers. (a) How many cubes are in one layer? (b) What is the volume of the packed cubes? (c) If 30 cubes are taken out, how many cubes are left? (5 marks)

54. Write the decimal 5.68 in a place value chart and say the place value of the 6 and of the 8. (4 marks)

55. Explain how you would find the lines of symmetry of a paper rectangle. How many are there? (4 marks)

56. Describe how to make a 1/2 L mark on an unmarked bottle using a 1 L container. (3 marks)

57. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Write an expression for what she has left and find it when d = 100. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 7
   28 ÷ 7 = 4 with nothing left over, so 7 is a factor of 28. The others leave a remainder.

2. D — 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 30. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30.

3. A — 19
   The rule is add 4. 15 + 4 = 19.

4. C — Hundreds
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 8 is in the hundreds place.

5. B — 3,450
   three thousand, four hundred and fifty: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 3,450.

6. D — 9,433
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,684 + 3,749 = 9,433.

7. D — 5,743
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

8. B — 3,425
   5,743 − 2,318 = 3,425. Check: 2,318 + 3,425 = 5,743.

9. C — add 500
   Each number is 500 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 500.

10. C — 9,794
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 7,305 + 2,489 = 9,794.

11. A — 5,280
   7,483 rounds to 7,480 and 2,196 rounds to 2,200. 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280.

12. B — 540
   27 × 2 = 54, then × 10 gives 540.

13. B — 630
   18 × 5 = 90 and 18 × 30 = 540. 90 + 540 = 630.

14. A — 800
   38 rounds to 40 and 22 rounds to 20. 40 × 20 = 800.

15. C — 8 remainder 5
   7 × 8 = 56 and 61 − 56 = 5. So 61 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 5. Check: 8 × 7 + 5 = 61.

16. B — 9 remainder 2
   9 × 9 = 81 and 83 − 81 = 2. So 83 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 9 + 2 = 83.

17. D — 5
   47 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 5. Each child gets 7 and 5 are left.

18. A — 3 2/5
   17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 2/5, so 17/5 = 3 2/5.

19. B — 0.70
   Adding a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value. 0.7 = 0.70.

20. C — 5
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 5.

21. C — 6c + 3d
   Only like terms can be joined. 2c + 3d + 4c = 6c + 3d.

22. D — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.

23. C — 6
   Layers = 48 ÷ 8 = 6.

24. A — Cuboid B
   A = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 blocks. B = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

25. A — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

26. A — 1 1/4 kg
   3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 kg.

27. A — Size does not tell us the mass
   We must measure to know the mass. Size alone does not tell us.

28. C — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

29. B — Towards the west
   The Sun rises in the east, so morning shadows point west.

30. D — Ksh 780
   Cost = number × price = 6 × 130 = Ksh 780.

31. B — Ksh 4,425
   Add the three costs: 1,200 + 2,350 + 875 = 4,425.

32. C — Ksh 495
   Add the three costs: 95 + 140 + 260 = 495.

33. D — Ksh 190
   100 + 50 + 20 + 20 = 190.

34. B — 800 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 8 = 8 × 100 = 800 cents.

35. C — The back wall
   A half turn takes you to face the opposite way.

36. D — a corner that is more closed than a square corner
   Its arms are closer together than the arms of a right angle.

37. A — Across the middle from side to side
   Folding across the middle makes the two halves match exactly. A diagonal does not, because the corners do not fit on each other.

38. A — mango
   The biggest number is 4, which belongs to mango.

39. D — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

40. A — 3
   5 − 2 = 3.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: five hundred and eighty-three
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for "five hundred and"; 1 mark for "eighty-three" spelt correctly with a hyphen.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 75 cm
   Working / marking points: 360 − 185 = 175 cm (2 marks); 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm (1 mark).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4,000, 3,750, 3,500 (rule: subtract 250)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three numbers.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: The book cover: 108 squares. The notebook: 100 squares. The book cover is larger by 8 squares.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for 108 and 100, 1 mark for the larger cover, 1 mark for 8.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 45 cm
   Working / marking points: 520 − 275 = 245 cm (2 marks); 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm (1 mark).

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 150 m (b) 144 m
   Working / marking points: (a) 45 + 30 + 45 + 30 = 150 m (2 marks for method, 1 mark for the answer with unit); (b) 2 × 3 = 6 m and 150 − 6 = 144 m (2 marks total, awarded 1 for 6 m and 1 for 144 m). Total 5 marks.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 4 L to 3 4/4 L (1 mark). 3 4/4 − 1 3/4 = 2 1/4 (1 mark). Check: 2 1/4 + 1 3/4 = 4 L (1 mark).

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: In a cube the length, width and height are equal. Example of a cube: a dice. Example of a cuboid that is not a cube: a matchbox or a brick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the property, 1 mark for each example.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 4,000 + 800 + 30 + 5 (b) 800 (c) 4,840 (d) odd because it ends in 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part; part (a) needs all four addends, part (b) 8 × 100, part (c) the ones digit 5 rounds up, part (d) needs the reason from the ones digit (1 mark for the classification plus reason together).

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,375 books. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the subtraction with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units, 1 mark for the check.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: 600 sweets
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (1 mark), then × 10 = 600 (1 mark).

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: 60 blocks; then 90 blocks
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (2 marks); 6 layers: 15 × 6 = 90 (2 marks).

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 40 cubes (b) 160 cubes (c) 130 cubes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8 × 5 = 40 (1 mark); (b) 40 × 4 = 160 (2 marks); (c) 160 − 30 = 130 (2 marks).

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ones 5, tenths 6, hundredths 8. The 6 is in the tenths place and the 8 is in the hundredths place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct chart, 1 mark for each place value, 1 mark for using the decimal point correctly.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fold the rectangle so that the two halves match. There are two folds that work: along the middle from top to bottom and along the middle from side to side. So there are 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding, 1 mark for halves matching, 1 mark for each of the two lines (or 2 marks for saying 2 with reasons).

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 1 L of water into one bottle. Share it into two identical bottles until the levels match. Mark the water level on one bottle as 1/2 L.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for starting with 1 L, 1 mark for sharing into two equal levels, 1 mark for marking 1/2 L.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: d − 45. When d = 100, she has 100 − 45 = 55 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for d − 45, 1 mark for the substitution, 1 mark for 55 shillings.
